subject: MAP: Benchmark evaluation exports + exec playbook
messages:
From: Jared Park <jared.park@acme-manufacturing.com>
To: naomi_feldman
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-manufacturing.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff / performance targets

Thanks Naomi — quick follow up from our side. To move the MAP along our infra team needs: a CSV of the benchmark results showing p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec throughput at 1/4/8/16 concurrent sessions, and the exact model variant + quantization used for each run. Can you also include a short set of slides (1–2 pages) that call out any anomalies and a dashboard link we can pin in our tracker?

High-level targets for us: p95 <= 300ms at 8 concurrent sessions for the 2k token prompt profile; sustained throughput >= 50k tokens/sec for batch workloads. If Redwood can't meet those in the MAP window we need to see fallback/rollout language in the MAP.

Appreciate a quick plan for deliverables and timing — we are trying to align procurement and engineering sign-off next Wed.

— Jared
Lead SRE, Acme Manufacturing

From: naomi_feldman
To: Jared Park <jared.park@acme-manufacturing.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-manufacturing.com>, marissa_cole, rishi_malhotra
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff / performance targets

Thanks Jared — plan below. Putting Marissa on the results packaging and Rishi on configuration notes.

Deliverables (ETA):
- CSV export with raw run-level metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, throughput tokens/sec, request size, concurrency, batch size) — due Wed 2027-03-03 EOD PT.
- 2-slide executive summary PDF calling out pass/fail vs Acme targets and recommended rollout (canary thresholds, fallback variants) — due Wed 2027-03-03 EOD PT.
- Shortlinks file with saved Grafana panels + Drive folder for raw logs — shared when CSV/slide are posted.
- A 30-min readout session (NA-friendly) proposed Thu 2027-03-04 10:00 AM PT.

Test config notes (summary):
- Models: redwood/open-70b (int8-quant) and redwood/open-13b (fp16) as the primary variants for the MAP.
- Workloads:
  * Prompt profile A: 2k tokens (padded seq), chat-style — target p95 <= 300ms at 8 concurrent.
  * Prompt profile B: 512 tokens, batched throughput test — target throughput >= 50k tokens/sec.
- Concurrency vector: 1, 4, 8, 16 sessions.
- TTFT measured as time from request accepted to first token emitted (p50/p95).

I'll attach a brief ops playbook for how we collected the runs. Marissa — can you confirm you can produce the CSV with the raw rows (one row per run) and the slides?

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole
To: naomi_feldman
Cc: rishi_malhotra, soojin_lee, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-manufacturing.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff / performance targets

On it — CSV schema below (I'll export as acme_map_benchmark_results.csv):
- run_id, model_variant, quant, batch_size, concurrency, prompt_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, ttft_ms, throughput_tokens_per_sec, failure_rate_pct, run_timestamp

Notes from initial runs:
- For open-70b int8 with KV cache warm and batch_size 8, we see p95=420ms at concurrency 8 for the 2k profile — slightly above Acme target. Increasing the pinned GPU memory + enabling continuous batching lowered p95 to ~290ms in a canary run. We'll include both runs and the config toggles used.
- Throughput tests (512 token profile) with open-13b fp16 sustained 62k tokens/sec at batch_size 16 across the pool of 4 workers.

Attachments I'll include in the folder: 20270303_acme-benchmark-summary-slides.pdf, acme_map_benchmark_results.csv, acme_dashboard_shortlinks.txt

Marissa Cole
Perf Engineering (Serving)
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-manufacturing.com>
To: naomi_feldman, marissa_cole
Cc: Jared Park <jared.park@acme-manufacturing.com>, procurement@acme-manufacturing.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff / performance targets

Thanks team — received the slides and CSV in the Drive link. Quick Q: can you call out which runs used the dedicated capacity vs hosted API? Procurement needs that explicitly to map pricing tiers for the MAP. Also please confirm whether any runs exceeded error_rate > 0.5%.

If the slides highlight the config that met our p95 target, that should be sufficient for sign-off; procurement will then ask for a short note in the MAP about fallback to the 13b variant for heavy concurrency windows.

— Priya
Head of Procurement, Acme Manufacturing

From: naomi_feldman
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-manufacturing.com>, Jared Park <jared.park@acme-manufacturing.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, rishi_malhotra, soojin_lee
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff / performance targets

Following up with the packaged deliverables — attached and summarized below. Posting the Drive/Grafana shortlinks here for your tracker.

Attachments:
- 20270303_acme-benchmark-summary-slides.pdf (2 pages): one page pass/fail dashboard vs your targets; one page recommended rollout with canary thresholds.
- acme_map_benchmark_results.csv (CSV): one row per run (schema shared earlier). Highlights: p95 <= 300ms achieved for the 2k prompt after enabling continuous batching + increasing pinned GPU memory on dedicated pool; TTFT p50 ~ 28ms for both variants when using the low-latency kernel path; sustained throughput 64.1k tokens/sec for the 512-token profile on open-13b (fp16).
- acme_dashboard_shortlinks.txt: contains the Grafana panel link and a saved query for the raw run traces.

Dedicated vs Hosted notes:
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) used for the primary pass/fail runs and for the low-latency canary. Hosted API runs were used for baseline comparison only. The CSV includes a "deployment_type" column marking each run as dedicated/hosted.

Failure rates:
- All critical runs for the MAP had failure_rate_pct <= 0.2%. We included an outlier set (warmup misconfig) with a 1.8% failure rate and noted the root cause in the slide footnote.

Next steps:
- Naomi to host a 30-min readout Thu 2027-03-04 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent).
- Procurement: if this meets your acceptance criteria we'll add the dedicated pool sizing and canary thresholds to the MAP doc and route for sign-off by EOD Fri.

Drive/Grafana links (short):
- https://drive.example/redwood/acme/benchmarks
- https://grafana.redwood.example/d/Acme123/latency-dashboard

Thanks — see you on the readout.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
